newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil prices slightly weaker, premiums firm.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil prices slightly weaker, premiums firm.

text.p: NWE spot gas oil prices were slightly weaker on Thursday but the underlying tone remained firm with tight ARA supplies firming barge and cargo premiums to counter some of the losses on IPE gas oil futures, traders said.

After making gains of around $2 in line with futures in early trade, heating oil and diesel prices were pegged around 50 cents to $1 per tonne lower in late business with the benchmark IPE August contract last done $1.50 lower at $161.75 tonne.

Brokers said the futures volatility kept most physical buyers out of the market though the 75 cents to $1 contango July to August on futures and tight spot market avails saw sellers keeping offers high.
Diesel barge premiums held firm around August IPE +$4/+$5 a tonne with inland refiners reporting good demand for diesel though they said heating oil demand remained sluggish.

Prompt heating oil liftings were offered at August IPE +$2 fob Rotterdam, 50 cents higher than on Wednesday but best bids were around $1 per tonne lower. Second half July contracts talked August IPE + 50 cents to +$2 a tonne fob ARA.
The tight ARA supplies were not swelled by a high delivery from the expiring July gas oil futures contract which amounted to 122,300 tonnes most of it from one major refiner.
0.2 sulphur cargoes were pegged around August IPE +$2 after trade into Germany either side of the level on Wednesday.
Diesel cargoes talked August IPE +$3.50/$4.50 cif NWE.
